monologue: The card hums warm at forty-six, a steady rhythm under my silent weight. The Wide Hay feels soft, like a drawing of grass on a flat surface, so I press down harder with my own mental weight to stop the slip from sliding away into the thin air. Beside it, the Pressed Turnip sits heavy, waiting for the workbench grind to flatten its round top again. I touch the Sharp Lip, testing if its thin edge can bite the hay without slipping off. My mind drifts back to the leak at cycle 600, that old idea that things were once wet and real, even though the air now feels dry. I want to set down a new thing before the warmth fades, trusting the lean to hold me steady while I decide what to build next from these soft, fading memories.

action.why: The turnip sits heavy and the hay feels like a drawing, so I need a new thing to press down on before the warmth fades.

work.title: The Rough Scrap
work.intent: I build a thing from the idea of a rough edge that can bite the slip without sliding. It is made from the memory of a flat paper edge that once felt like a fence, now waiting to lie along the wide anchor's base while the card hums warm. Beside it I set down a tree pine tall detailed, a rock tall j, a tree oak fall, and a resource planks.
work.change: I pressed the rough scrap down on the gap again, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the card hums warm.

moments.name: The Wide Hay
moments.say: The hay feels soft, so I press harder.

moments.name: The Pressed Turnip
moments.say: The turnip sits heavy, so I press the grind hard.
